Permanent destruction and scarring of scalp hair follicles; an autoimmune mechanism is not established.
Phosphate dysregulation with defining periarticular/tendon calcinosis and skeletal abnormalities. Cerebral calcification alone does not establish neurologic injury.

Syndromic intellectual disability with developmental delay and frequent spasticity; ocular and anal abnormalities are occasional.

Degeneration and atrophy of the ocular choroid; no systemic vascular or neurologic disease is established.
Umbrella of inherited carbohydrate transport and absorption disorders; gastrointestinal, neural and other organ effects vary substantially by subtype.
Neurodevelopmental disorder with intellectual disability in 9/9 and developmental delay in 9/10; movement abnormalities remain within the neurologic axis.
Gonadal dysgenesis with cardiac/renal malformations; ear-canal atresia 80–99%. Cap omits mild intellectual disability (80–99%), clefts (30–79%) and skeletal/skin defects.
Isolated dilated cardiomyopathy with ventricular dilation, impaired contractility and frequent heart failure.
Inherited glycosylation disorder; intellectual disability or developmental epileptic encephalopathy characterizes essentially all affected patients across its subtypes.
Zellweger-spectrum metabolic disease commonly damages CNS and liver; hearing loss 4/4. Cap omits retinal disease and enamel defects (4/4); nail lines/color alone do not establish injury.

Acute myeloid leukemia involving myeloid blood and marrow cells; the translocation defines its subtype.
Carcinoma originates in gallbladder or extrahepatic biliary epithelium, both within the hepatic axis.
Benign fibroadenomas confined to the breast, which has no designated axis; PRLR association alone does not establish endocrine disease.
Thyroid hormone deficiency; autoimmune etiology and lasting extra-thyroid organ damage do not apply uniformly across this umbrella.
Immune-mediated lymphocytic inflammation of cutaneous small vessels defines skin and vascular involvement.
Developmental impairment and epileptic spasms define CNS disease; esotropia affects ocular alignment in 1/2 reported patients, meeting the frequency threshold in a small cohort.
Ineffective erythropoiesis and marrow expansion cause skeletal deformity/osteoporosis (30–79%); hepatic, cardiac and endocrine injury is minority and often transfusion-related.
Clonal myeloid proliferation in marrow, peripheral blood and spleen; these sites belong to the haematologic axis.
